clue.text: 24's clue is frontal

parts.note: the clue to 24-across reads 'The setter as object', and the setter as object is me
the same clue's 'subject' gives topic

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the clue to entry 24 is blunt and in-your-face.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue to 24-across, 'The setter as object and subject', is read again here: the setter as object is ME and a subject is a TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Metopic is the anatomical adjective for the forehead, as in the metopic suture, so it means frontal.

clue.text: Fairy godmother's piece

indicators.note: a piece of the word godmother's is a short run of its letters taken from inside it

explanation.surface: A fairy godmother's party piece, perhaps her wand-waving trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Moth is one of Titania's fairies in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, the theme linking this clue with 4 and 26.
explanation.definitionFit: In A Midsummer Night's Dream one of Titania's attendant sprites bears this name, so it is a fairy.

clue.text: Humble opinion on moth with a drink?

parts.note: someone's take on a matter is their opinion of it
the fairy Moth is the answer at 1-down, so moth can stand for 'one down'
a peg is a measure of spirits, an old colonial word for a drink

explanation.surface: A modest view expressed about a moth that is having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' and 'with' are link words placing the pieces in order. Moth is replaced by the grid reference of its light, 1-down, written as ONE DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble a proud person is idiomatically to reduce their standing by one notch, as on a peg.

clue.text: Hair in German place going into the ears?

indicators.note: what goes into the ears is heard, so a spoken form is wanted

parts.note: Platz is the German word for a place or square

explanation.surface: A question whether some German location has found its way into somebody's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAITS here is said with the older short vowel, 'plats', which matches the German Platz.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaits are braided lengths of hair, so the word stands for hair arranged that way.

clue.text: Fairy, a nut on the Internet?

parts.note: a cob or cobnut is a kind of hazelnut
the web is the World Wide Web, the Internet in everyday speech

explanation.surface: A fairy described as an eccentric person who is always online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link word joining the two pieces. Cobweb is another of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare gives Titania an attendant sprite with this name in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Surviving from a scuffle, ancestor of Scottish kings

definitions.text: Surviving from a scuffle, ancestor of Scottish kings

indicators.note: the answer is taken from a run of letters straddling these two words

explanation.surface: A boy escapes alive from a fight and goes on to found a royal line.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes Banquo's son in Macbeth, who flees the murderers and was held to be forefather of the Stewart kings; his name also straddles 'scuffle, ancestor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Banquo's son in Macbeth survives the ambush and was held to found the Stewart royal line.

clue.text: This is 4, G-man to admit having grabbed it

indicators.note: the agent grabs the number, so the numeral goes inside his letters

parts.note: a G-man is an American FBI agent, informally a fed
the number four in Roman numerals is IV
to own something is to admit or confess it

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark that this is number four, with a federal agent confessing after seizing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the clue itself, which is the five-down clue. 'It' simply points back to the 4.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is self-referential: 'this' is the very entry being solved, located at grid position five down.

clue.text: Albert losing head over heartless lady is in a bad way

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting over another comes first
the first letter is dropped from the surname

parts.note: Albert Herring is the title character of Benjamin Britten's comic opera

indicators.note: the middle letters are removed from the word lady, leaving its outside

explanation.surface: A man called Albert, having lost his mind over a cold-hearted woman, is in a sorry state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Albert' leads to Britten's opera Albert Herring; 'losing head' gives ERRING. 'Heartless' strips AD from lady to leave LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a bad way is doing it wrongly, which is the sense of the adverb from err.

clue.text: Near to rubbish drinker: he's in a film with three brothers

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near
tat is cheap rubbish or junk

indicators.note: the first word is put inside the drinker

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker
the word he taken as written

explanation.surface: Something close by the junk-loving boozer, who appears in a picture with three siblings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' and the leftover words link the pieces. The film is the 1935 Marx Brothers comedy, starring Groucho, Chico and Harpo.
explanation.definitionFit: A Night at the Opera is a famous comedy film starring the three Marx Brothers.

clue.text: Unknown females first found in the East — go gently …

indicators.note: these pieces are found inside the word for the compass direction

parts.note: east is the compass direction
in algebra an unknown is x, y or z; here y
does are female deer or rabbits
first can be the Roman numeral I, number one

explanation.surface: Mysterious women first came across somewhere in the Orient, travelling slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 12-down, whose 'on the other hand' answers this clue's East.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a common spoken instruction to move or act with care and without haste.

clue.text: Such a dish at heart of report?

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: ticker is informal slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A question whether a certain dish lies at the centre of some account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At' is a link word. 'Heart' looks like an instruction to take middle letters of report, but it gives TICKER, which is then said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: Tikka is a South Asian dish of marinated pieces of meat cooked in a clay oven.

clue.text: Bearded man, missing a long time, drinks

indicators.note: the letter a goes missing from the slang word

parts.note: beaver is old slang for a man with a beard
ages is an everyday word for a long time

explanation.surface: A man with a beard who has gone missing for ages is having drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearded man' is old slang that most solvers will not know: a beaver was a man with a beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Beverages are drinks of any kind, the word being a slightly formal synonym.

clue.text: Football club with little money? Then demand it gets new diet

parts.note: a sou was an old French coin of small value, so a tiny sum
taken as written
to dun someone is to demand payment from them

indicators.note: new letters mean the word diet is rearranged

explanation.surface: A struggling football club, short of money, insists that its players adopt a new diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It gets' is a link. 'New' rearranges DIET as ITED. Southend United is a football club from Southend-on-Sea in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: Southend United is an English professional football club based in Essex, nicknamed the Shrimpers.

clue.text: … on the other hand, home finishes over the ocean

parts.note: following the East of 8-down, the other side of the compass is west
to be in is to be at home
something that dies finishes or ends

explanation.surface: A continuation of the previous remark: by contrast, a house comes to an end out across the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 8-down, where EAST surrounded the other pieces; here the opposite direction starts the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, the Caribbean islands lie across the Atlantic, over the ocean.

clue.text: Woman's right, always

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, stands for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman's entitlement, now and for good.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb used in 'for good' or 'at all times' is a direct synonym for always.

clue.text: Apply it with trowel to engine of such capacity

indicators.note: applying the words with a trowel smears and rearranges them, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to slap something on with a trowel, followed by a mention of an engine size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apply' is an unusual anagram sign, meaning work over the letters of IT and TROWEL. 'To engine' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine of two litres capacity is described by the compound adjective formed from the size.

clue.text: Religious leader that eats core 6

indicators.note: the word that eats the other letters, holding them inside
the answer to 6-down means 'in a bad way', so the letters of core are put in a bad order

explanation.surface: A religious leader described as someone who eats the core of something.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6-down, meaning wrongly, used as the anagram signal on CORE to make EOCR inside THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A theocrat rules in the name of God, a priestly ruler, so a religious leader.

clue.text: Crafty as a plan to produce cloth on river in Aberdeen

indicators.note: in a down entry, the cloth sitting on the river comes below it

parts.note: the River Dee reaches the sea at Aberdeen in Scotland
plaid is a woollen tartan cloth

explanation.surface: A scheme to make woollen cloth beside a Scottish river is cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To produce' is a link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-laid plan is carefully and secretly prepared, so crafty.

clue.text: Work hard in essays to get prizes

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for essays

parts.note: an essay is an attempt or try
op is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A student slogs at essays in hope of winning awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essays' means attempts, not written compositions.
explanation.definitionFit: Trophies are cups or similar awards given as prizes.

clue.text: Oriental with air force units

indicators.note: the words with air are forced into smaller units, a run of their letters giving the answer

explanation.surface: An Asian person linked with air force formations.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the words 'with air'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai person comes from Thailand in South-East Asia, so is Oriental in the old usage.

clue.text: Time taken in introduction, not for 13

indicators.note: the abbreviation is taken inside the word for introduction

parts.note: a proem is a preface or introduction

explanation.surface: A remark that time is used up in the opening, but not permanently.
explanation.walkthrough: '13' refers to the answer at 13-across, meaning always.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag means for the time being, temporarily, the opposite of permanently.

clue.text: Good person to get at American position

parts.note: St, saint, is a good person

explanation.surface: A virtuous person gets the better of an American over rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or position in society.

clue.text: Race in which Gary follows on induces passive resistance

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed inside the word for race

parts.note: a nation is a race or people

indicators.note: the actor's surname comes after the word on

parts.note: taken as written
Gary Cooper was the American film star of High Noon

explanation.surface: A race in which Gary trails behind provokes a peaceful protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Induces' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to cooperate with authority is the classic form of passive resistance.

clue.text: See 26
It's crucial to get a social worker from abroad

parts.note: an import is something brought in from abroad
an ant is a social insect, a worker in its colony

explanation.surface: Hiring a care worker from overseas is said to be vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare job, but it is the ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something important matters greatly, so is crucial.

clue.text: The setter as object and subject

parts.note: the setter speaks of himself in the object case as me

explanation.surface: A setter talks about himself as both the object and the subject of a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' and 'subject' suggest grammar, but object is ME and subject is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject of a talk or piece of writing.

clue.text: Express regret for boy with vision

parts.note: to sigh is to express regret or sorrow
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Feeling sorry for a lad who can see.
explanation.definitionFit: A sighted person can see, as opposed to someone blind.

clue.text: Fairy has to read editor's rubbish

parts.note: must means has to

indicators.note: rubbish here means the letters are messed up

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A fairy is obliged to read the editor's junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' rearranges READ with EDS to make ARDSEED. Mustardseed is one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Mustardseed is one of Titania's attendant sprites in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
